_what: The words of each thing the device this page runs in can do by itself and the person turns on or off here (src/workspace/device-switch.tsx). The Trillion iPhone app says which switches it has (window.__trillionSwitches, { id: device }), takes { id, command } on its trillionSwitch bridge and tells each switch's state ({ id, on, waiting, sent, sending, problem }) in the trillion-native-switch event (ios/App/DeviceSwitch.swift). Each row: `id` as the device names it, the `place` it shows on, its `title`, and `said`, the line under the title for each state, in this order, the first that holds: the device's own problem, `off`, `sending` (while it sends), `waiting` (some wait to be sent), `on`. {device}, {waiting} and {sent} are filled from the device and its state. A switch the device has but no row names is not shown.

switches.title: Send photos and videos from this {device}'s Photos

said.off: New photos and videos go to Files under Recordings > Cameras, on any connection, also with Trillion in the background. Items from the last 14 days come too, even when Photos keeps the originals only in iCloud.
said.waiting: {waiting} waiting. They go up by themselves when this {device} is back online.
said.on: On. {sent} sent so far. New photos and videos, and those from the 14 days before you turned this on, go to Files under Recordings > Cameras.
